question.question: Can VerifyLeader return nil on a partitioned old leader after the remaining voters elected a higher-term replacement and completed a command before the verification invocation, while only a nonvoter remains reachable from the old leader?
question.importance: VerifyLeader is documented as ensuring continuing leadership and preventing stale FSM reads. A false positive after a newer leader has completed a write would invalidate that authority check; this question does not assume the application actually performs a stale read.
contexts: Old leader separated from voting peers while nonvoter remains connected
New leader command completion precedes old VerifyLeader invocation
Lease and negative-response workers remain enabled
event_paths: Real bootstrap -> public AddVoter transitions -> stable configuration -> link partition -> replacement leader election -> successful Apply -> old VerifyLeader -> public future completion

supporting_behavior_ids.B_verify_register: Initializes voter threshold and registers all replication workers.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_member_activation: Produces stable voter/nonvoter membership through public changes.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_lease_check: Independent voter-only protection that must remain running in the witness.

counterevidence: Lease check counts only voters and eventually steps down an isolated leader.
A negative peer response can abort verification before affirmative count reaches threshold.
Commitment itself ignores nonvoter match indexes.
unknowns: The proposed real same-execution prefix and public verification endpoint remain to be executed.
The stale-read application consequence is excluded unless separately observed.
Different per-node timeouts must pass actual configuration validation and leave protective workers enabled.
question.trigger_rationale: Source shows voter-derived verification threshold combined with registration of all replication workers and identity-free vote increments. A source asymmetry alone is insufficient; select authority invalidation by an actual newer leader write as the discriminator.

obligation.description: VerifyLeader invoked on an old leader after a replacement leader in a strictly higher term has successfully completed Apply must not return success, while the old leader has not regained leadership and membership remains unchanged.

scope.description: Same-cluster authority check after a higher-term replacement leader completes a write before invocation; stable three-voter plus one-nonvoter membership and finite link partition, no process restart or Byzantine data.
assumptions: A successful replacement Apply and higher term are observed before verification admission.
No membership change or old-leader re-election occurs during the observed interval.
All protocol workers including leader lease checks continue under configured legal timeouts.
excluded: Actual application stale read unless observed
Reusing server identity or fabricating responses

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader documents ensuring the peer is still leader and preventing stale FSM reads. A successful write by a higher-term replacement before invocation establishes a stronger invalidation prefix than loss of connectivity alone. If the old node has not regained authority, success is incompatible with that API responsibility. Nonvoter registration is a candidate mechanism, not the normative source.
alternatives: Voter-only lease and negative responses may prevent success; keep them running and observe the actual result.
unresolved: Real producer/election/Apply/VerifyLeader same-history evidence is required.

bindings.description: Public verification contract and leader-loop future completion under review.

associations.rationale: Public contract requires current leadership; leader-loop completion returns the observed future status.

rationale: Membership investigation found an A2 eligibility asymmetry: commitment and lease filter voters, verification registration does not. Preserve that sourced observation without declaring an unsafe decision. Select a bounded real-history check using a replacement leader completed write before old-node verification, retaining all protective workers. This has greater safety value than another local eligibility counter comparison or stale AddVoter documentation mismatch.
